coverage_notes: SOURCES: Teams recording 0-3937 s (her lapel mic; whisper en + ar passes read end to end, word timestamps used for every span) + phone recording (room audio; en + ar passes). MEASURED OFFSET phone_t = teams_t + 738.7 s (five anchor words agree within 0.2 s; the brief's +742 is about 3 s off). The phone ends at teams-time ~3915, so the Teams file is the only record of the last ~20 s. PHONE-ONLY STRETCH (phone 0-739 s): no Arabic was taught - students practicing numbers 0-8 before class, her 'Marhaba!' greeting (phone 201.7 s), prayer requests and prayer, then Global Focus Week guest speakers in English (Frontiers; ELIC / Mission Go). The phone was also used inside the Teams hour to recover words the Teams passes dropped (jaaruki / jaaruka / jaaruhu, jadiid at 448 and 2560, raqm waaHid, ithnayn, the 'laa / laa shukran / full sentence' exchange). Spans derived that way are given in TEAMS time; a few phone-file alternates are included. SCREEN SHARE: yes. Her laptop screen shows the Top Hat attendance page from ~42 s to 2232 s (the whole letter lesson), then the 'Unit 4 Vocab (2)' PowerPoint (18 slides, Arabic on every slide, read at full resolution - these are the spelling authority for the vocab list), then attendance again at the end. The letter work was done on a PHYSICAL whiteboard that is only visible in the room-camera picture-in-picture (230x145 px): letter shapes can be confirmed (د ـد / ذ ـذ, د+ج+ا+ج=دجاج, ذ+ب+ا+ب=ذباب, ي+ذ+و+ب=يذوب, ذ+ا+ت=ذات, أ+خ+ذ+ت) but vowel marks are unreadable. Board-word vowels therefore come from the book: they are exactly the Writing د words (p.78: دَجاج، جَديد) and Writing ذ words (p.80: ذُباب، خُذ، أَخَذْتُ، يَذوب، ذات). The listening items are Unit 4 Listening Exercise 5 (p.77; Lingco LE5-01..06 audio exists) and LE6 (LE6-01 ذُباب, 02 ذات, 04 خُذ). Frames sampled every 3 s over the whole video (1312 frames), de-duplicated on the screen area; 18 slide frames + 8 upscaled PiP board crops saved in ~/arabic-catchup/frames/2026-09-29/. SPELLING: slide > Lingco/book (u04_0067-0083 = the slide list; book p.86) > own knowledge (flagged). Full vowels completed from the book where the slide shows fewer (e.g. slide تُحِبّين -> book تُحِبِّين). QUIZ: she made NO announcement about the Unit 1-4 vocab/matching quiz or the writing quiz - no date, no format. Both passes of both recordings were searched (quiz / exam / test / dictation / matching / grade / Friday / Monday / next week). Related things she did say: (1) 'let's say ON THE EXAM you forgot [the ending]... go to a noun you know really well [baab, ism, kitaab] and conjugate it, then apply those suffixes' (3094 s) - so possessive / cinda endings are exam material; (2) 'when you do your ORAL ASSESSMENT, because she's speaking in Shami, she's going to ask you about your nimrit tilifuun' (3466 s) - a Shaami-speaking tutor runs an oral assessment; (3) 'Go with Fabiola, the tutor... let's do possessive pronouns' with baab, ism, kitaab, jaar (2515 s); (4) Thursday 10/1: 'I'll give you some time until Thursday to process those two letters before I introduce two more [raa', zaay]... we have a lot of drills to write next time' and 'practice these words until Thursday so we can speak a little bit'; (5) 'in this class they're teaching only the singular; in 102 we'll teach the plural'; (6) 'from this moment onward, if you have a question, you have to say ustaadha, cindii su'aal'. SPEAKERS: the Teams lapel mic favours her, but in round-the-room drills the first token of a pair is often the student; those are listed as not_her_spans where identifiable. Deliberate mistakes (ind with hamza, Hibb, jaamica jadiid, 'not dhu') are marked not_her_spans with who='deliberate mistake'.

'In Arabic we call it by the country': khubz caraaqii (Iraqi - boat-shaped, thick, one layer), khubz suurii (Syrian - flat, two layers), khubz lubnaanii (Lebanese - the thinnest, two very thin layers), khubz maSrii (Egyptian - thicker). The adjective comes after khubz.

Board spelling drill: daal + jiim + alif + jiim. First daal = independent form (nothing before it); jiim = initial; alif = connecting; last jiim = independent, because alif never connects to the left.
Her jiim often sounds like the s in 'pleasure' (zh) - a Levantine habit (Teams even heard 'the zaz'); the formal jiim is j.

letters.notes: NEW TODAY (daal). 'The first one, we call it daal.' Connects only to the right, like alif and waaw, so it has only two forms: independent and connecting ('how many forms should we have? Two'). An initial daal is just the independent form ('connecting - we have nothing to connect'). Height: 'alif is the tallest; daal is somewhere between alif and baa'; the tooth [of baa'] is the shortest - make sure you do these differences.' Angle: 'should we write it like a 90 degree angle or like 60 degree angle? That's up to you... just make sure it is not similar to the tooth. I care about the height more.' After a daal the next letter starts over in its initial form ('you cannot make a connection... treat it like the alif and the waaw'): jadiid = jiim + daal + INITIAL yaa' + daal. In Huduud the first daal is connecting (Haa' connects on both sides) and the last is independent (after waaw). Sound: 'the sound of D, the English D, so we're not going to spend much time with the pronunciation.' Words: dajaaj, jadiid, khuduud, Huduud, adab (+ aHdaath, Listening Exercise 5 item 6, not read).

her_clear_utterances.context: 'the first one, we call it daal'

letters.notes: NEW TODAY (dhaal). 'The transliteration for the dhaal is a dh, small dh. The capital [DH] is for another letter' (ظ). 'Written similar to the daal, the only difference is the dot... daal without, dhaal with - you could remember it that way: dhaal with a dot. They connect the same way, they act the same way, just the sounding of course is different.' Sound = th in 'other' (vs ث, th in 'three'): 'In English, we have TH for both sounds. Do you remember early in the semester you did one drill... is it a th sound or a dh sound? So now you learn the two characters.' Board words (book p.80): dhubaab (flies), khudh (take!), akhadhtu (I took - dhaal with SUKUUN, 'not dhu'), yadhuub (it melts), dhaat (same/self).

her_clear_utterances.context: dh-sound syllables (dha, dhu, dhi) - which set is ث vs ذ is inferred

letters.notes: 'alif is tall, the tallest' - the height reference for daal. Alif and waaw were the first 'connect only to the right' letters; daal and dhaal join them today. Because alif never connects to the left, the letter after it starts again (final jiim of dajaaj = independent; final baa' of dhubaab = independent). At the start of akhadhtu it carries the hamza with fatHa.

Height reference: 'if I'm writing on the line, baa' for instance is this' - its tooth is the shortest; daal must be taller than the tooth. In dhubaab: initial baa' after dhaal (dhaal doesn't connect left), final baa' independent after alif.
